name: Common Mallow

facts.what: Leaves and the round green seed 'cheeses'
facts.how: Leaves raw or cooked; the mucilage thickens soups
facts.value: Vitamins A and C; a natural thickener

caution: A safe, mild, very common plant; harvest away from sprayed ground. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Identification
sections.body: Round scalloped leaves and small pale flowers, with flat button-like green fruits kids have long called 'cheeses.' A wild cousin of okra and hibiscus.

sections.title: In the kitchen
sections.body: Mild leaves for salad or pot, and a mucilage that thickens soups like okra. The green 'cheeses' are a fun raw nibble.
